claim: eiCompare implements and directly compares three distinct ecological-inference estimator families for the same precinct-level dataset: Goodman's ecological regression (fast, deterministic baseline), King's (1997) iterative Bayesian 2x2 EI, and RxC multinomial-Dirichlet EI for simultaneous multi-candidate/multi-group estimation -- giving practitioners a built-in method-sensitivity check.
stance_target: state of the art in ecological-inference tooling; usefulness of running multiple EI estimators in parallel to bound uncertainty from model choice, relevant to matrices de transfert axis of the French projection methodology gradient
scope_conditions: R package, wraps `ei` and `eiPack` packages; general statistical methods portable beyond the US racial-voting context
quoted_support: The package provides three EI methods: Goodman's Regression (ei_good()) -- A fast, deterministic method based on ecological regression. Useful as a baseline estimate. Iterative EI (ei_iter()) -- King's (1997) iterative 2x2 ecological inference method with Bayesian estimation. RxC EI (ei_rxc()) -- Multinomial-Dirichlet model for simultaneous estimation across all race-candidate pairs.

claim: eiCompare's stated target user base explicitly includes grassroots/local organizations seeking data-driven local targeting tools to inform advocacy actions -- the same 'field organizing prioritization' use case as the French research query, but applied to racially polarized voting rather than partisan bloc vote projection.
stance_target: precedent for ecological-inference tooling being purpose-built for grassroots/local-action targeting, not just litigation or forecasting
scope_conditions: US context; stated design intent, not empirical usage data
quoted_support: eiCompare was built with several types of users in mind: ... Grassroots organizations looking for data-driven tools to fuel their fight against vote dilution at the local level.

claim: eiCompare supports VAP-denominator (voting-age-population) normalization via rpv_normalize(), allowing EI estimates originally computed against total voting-age population to be re-conditioned on actual voters only -- addressing a known methodological choice-point (turnout vs. eligible population as denominator) in ecological inference of vote shares.
stance_target: methodological nuance in ecological-inference implementations relevant to choosing turnout base for bureau-de-vote projections
quoted_support: When using voting age population (VAP) as the denominator (instead of total votes), use rpv_normalize() to condition estimates on voters only
